\chapter{Learning Theory — Bernstein}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.JohnsonLindenstrauss.Bernstein
\section{Overview}

This module develops a two-parameter sub-exponential MGF condition,
\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}, and derives from it
one-sided, other-sided, and two-sided Bernstein-type concentration
inequalities.  The main application is a tail bound for the deviation
of $\sum_i Y_i^2$ from its mean $n\sigma^2$ for an independent
identically-distributed family, which serves as the central reusable
tool for Johnson--Lindenstrauss-style concentration arguments.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Bernstein MGF condition]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}
\label{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}
\leanok
$\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}\ X\ \mu\ c\ t_{\max}$ is a
predicate on a random variable $X : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$, a measure
$\mu$, and real parameters $c, t_{\max} \ge 0$.  It asserts that for
every $t$ with $|t| \le t_{\max}$, the exponential moment
$e^{tX}$ is $\mu$-integrable, and the moment generating function
satisfies $\mathbf{E}_\mu[e^{tX}] \le e^{c t^2}$.  The pair
$(c, t_{\max})$ parametrizes a ``two-parameter sub-exponential'' family:
$c$ controls the quadratic growth near zero and $t_{\max}$ bounds the
radius of validity.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[iid closure of the Bernstein MGF condition]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.sum_of_iIndepFun}
\label{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.sum_of_iIndepFun}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\{X_i\}_{i \in s}$ be a mutually independent family of measurable
real random variables on a probability space, each satisfying
$\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}\ (X_i)\ \mu\ c_i\ t_{\max}$ for
a common radius $t_{\max}$.  Then the finite sum
$\sum_{i \in s} X_i$ satisfies
$\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}\ (\sum_{i\in s} X_i)\ \mu\ (\sum_{i\in s} c_i)\ t_{\max}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Upper-tail Bernstein bound]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_ge_le}
\label{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_ge_le}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$ satisfy $\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}\ X\ \mu\ c\ t_{\max}$
with $c > 0$.  For every $s$ with $0 \le s \le 2c\,t_{\max}$,
\[
  \mu\bigl(\{\omega \mid s \le X(\omega)\}\bigr) \;\le\;
  \exp\!\Bigl(-\tfrac{s^2}{4c}\Bigr).
\]
The condition $s \le 2c\,t_{\max}$ ensures that the Chernoff-optimal
parameter $t = s/(2c)$ lies in the validity region $|t| \le t_{\max}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lower-tail Bernstein bound]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_le_le}
\label{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_le_le}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$ satisfy $\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}\ X\ \mu\ c\ t_{\max}$
with $c > 0$.  For every $s$ with $0 \le s \le 2c\,t_{\max}$,
\[
  \mu\bigl(\{\omega \mid X(\omega) \le -s\}\bigr) \;\le\;
  \exp\!\Bigl(-\tfrac{s^2}{4c}\Bigr).
\]
This is the symmetric lower-tail analogue of
$\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure\_ge\_le}$,
obtained by applying the upper-tail bound to $-X$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Two-sided Bernstein bound]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_abs_gt_le}
\label{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_abs_gt_le}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF, ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_ge_le, ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_le_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$ satisfy $\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}\ X\ \mu\ c\ t_{\max}$
with $c > 0$.  For every $s$ with $0 \le s \le 2c\,t_{\max}$,
\[
  \mu\bigl(\{\omega \mid s < |X(\omega)|\}\bigr) \;\le\;
  2\exp\!\Bigl(-\tfrac{s^2}{4c}\Bigr).
\]
The bound follows by combining the upper- and lower-tail bounds via a
union bound.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Centered squared iid Bernstein tail bound]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.centered_squared_iid_tail}
\label{ProbabilityTheory.centered_squared_iid_tail}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF, ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_abs_gt_le, ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.sum_of_iIndepFun}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\{Y_i\}_{i \in \iota}$ be a mutually independent, identically
distributed family of measurable real random variables on a probability
space $(\Omega, \mu)$, where $|\iota| = n$.  Suppose that for each $i$
the centered square $Y_i^2 - \sigma^2$ satisfies
$\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}\ (Y_i^2 - \sigma^2)\ \mu\ c\ t_{\max}$
with $c > 0$.  Then for every $s$ with
$0 \le s \le 2n c\, t_{\max}$,
\[
  \mu\!\left(\left\{\omega \;\middle|\;
    s < \left|\sum_{i} Y_i(\omega)^2 - n\sigma^2\right|\right\}\right)
  \;\le\;
  2\exp\!\Bigl(-\tfrac{s^2}{4nc}\Bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}
